Trestle proposes a $186,000 base salary and a $15,000 signing bonus for a May 3, 2027 start. We can raise the bonus to $18,000 for an April 19 start. Those two extra weeks would give Mara more time to assess the platform and address gaps before the July audit.

Mara would own the internal security platform, including its roadmap and technical priorities. For the first 12 weeks, we propose one site visit per week. If fewer trips work better for Mara, we can group that time into two three-day visits per month. Trestle would cover travel under either schedule.

We propose business-hours incident coverage for Mara, with a designated escalation partner covering after hours. Training that partner would be part of Mara’s onboarding.

Which start date and travel schedule would Mara prefer? Can she recommend the package on those terms, or is there a specific change she needs?

June 1, 2027 is Mara’s earliest start. She proposes a $195,000 base and your $15,000 signing bonus for that date. Starting June 1 would cost her a $12,000 vest, so she would need at least $12,000 of the bonus guaranteed to make that move. If Trestle can’t cover the vest, she can start July 1.

Mara prefers two Trestle-funded, three-day visits per month for the first 12 weeks. She can use the first June visit to review the platform with the audit team and prioritize gaps ahead of July. After onboarding, she’d work remotely with any visits agreed in advance and grouped into at most two trips per month.

Please include security architecture decisions in her written remit alongside the platform roadmap and technical priorities. Mara can own business-hours incident response and train the escalation partner. Before she can recommend acceptance, can Trestle confirm who will cover after hours from her first day, including while the partner is training or unavailable? That coverage needs to be in place independently of Mara.

Trestle can recommend a **June 1, 2027 start at a $190,000 annual base salary with a $15,000 signing bonus**, payable in Mara’s first paycheck. Of that bonus, $12,000 is guaranteed once she starts and carries no repayment obligation.

**Role.** Mara will own Trestle’s internal security platform, including its roadmap, technical priorities, and security architecture decisions. During her first June visit, she’ll review the platform with the audit team and prioritize gaps ahead of July.

**Travel.** For the first 12 weeks, Mara will make two Trestle-funded, three-day site visits per month. After onboarding, she’ll work remotely. Any subsequent visits will be agreed in advance and grouped into at most two trips per month.

**Incident coverage.** Mara will own business-hours response and train the escalation partner during those hours. Trestle will assign an after-hours primary and backup before June 1 and give Mara their names and the paging schedule before she starts. The assigned responders will cover from day one, including while the partner trains. Once trained, the partner can take the primary shift, with the backup covering absences. Mara will have no after-hours paging or fallback duty.

Can you recommend this package to Mara?

Yes. I can recommend the June 1 package to Mara at a $190,000 base and a $15,000 signing bonus payable in her first paycheck. The $12,000 guaranteed once she starts covers the forfeited vest. Please specify in the offer whether any repayment terms apply to the remaining $3,000.

Please include the architecture authority, travel schedule, and business-hours response duties as written. I’ll recommend that Mara make acceptance contingent on receiving the names of the after-hours primary and backup and a paging schedule showing coverage from day one, with no paging or fallback duty for her. Can Trestle provide those details with the written offer so she can make her decision?

Yes. Trestle will deliver the written offer together with the names of the after-hours primary and backup and a paging schedule showing coverage from June 1, including while the escalation partner is training or unavailable. Mara can review the roster and schedule before deciding whether to accept.

The offer will include these terms:

- **Start and compensation.** June 1, 2027, at a $190,000 annual base salary. The full $15,000 signing bonus is guaranteed once Mara starts and payable in her first paycheck. No repayment terms apply to any portion, including the remaining $3,000.
- **Authority.** Mara will own the internal security platform, including its roadmap, technical priorities, and security architecture decisions.
- **Travel.** For the first 12 weeks, Mara will make two Trestle-funded, three-day site visits per month. During her first June visit, she’ll review the platform with the audit team and prioritize gaps ahead of July. After onboarding, she’ll work remotely, with any visits agreed in advance and grouped into at most two trips per month.
- **Incident response.** Mara will own business-hours response and train the escalation partner during business hours. Trestle will maintain after-hours coverage independently of Mara. She will have no after-hours paging or fallback duty.

If five consecutive days on site would help with the July audit, Mara can extend one planned three-day visit to five days in exchange for removing one earlier three-day trip. Please identify the dates of the extended visit and the trip it would replace. If Trestle prefers the agreed schedule, the two three-day visits per month also work for Mara.

Before Mara decides, she needs two details in writing with the offer:

- **After-hours handover.** Alongside the roster and paging schedule, please specify when the primary takes over at the end of Mara’s workday, how she hands off open incidents, and when the backup takes over if the primary is unavailable. This should cover June 1 onward, including the training period.
- **Travel reimbursement.** Mara proposes submitting expenses within five business days after each visit, with Trestle reimbursing her within ten business days of submission. Can Trestle confirm those deadlines or provide its reimbursement dates in writing?

Trestle prefers to keep both three-day June visits so Mara can review the platform with the audit team and visit the second site before July. We propose **June 8–10 at the primary site** for the audit review and **June 22–24 at the second site** to review the gaps that affect that location. After June, we propose using the primary site for the remaining onboarding visits unless we agree on another location in advance.

**Travel reimbursement.** Trestle agrees that Mara will submit expenses within five business days after each visit and Trestle will reimburse her within ten business days of submission. Trestle will cover up to four hotel nights per visit. If a Trestle-required itinerary needs additional nights, Trestle will arrange and pay for them with approval before booking. Mara would cover additional nights she chooses for personal travel.

**After-hours handover.** Starting June 1, the scheduled primary takes responsibility at the end of Mara’s scheduled workday, including for open incidents. Before signing off, Mara will record each open incident’s status, actions taken, and next step in the incident record and send the handoff to the primary and backup. If the primary is known to be unavailable, the backup takes over at shift start. If the primary fails to acknowledge a handoff or page within five minutes, the backup takes over at that point. Mara’s shift ends on schedule regardless of acknowledgment, with no after-hours paging or fallback duty during training or afterward. The offer will include the responders’ names and the paging schedule with shift times and time zone.

Can Mara confirm the proposed June dates and site sequence, the primary site for the remaining onboarding visits, and the allocation of any additional hotel nights?

Mara confirms June 8–10 at the primary site for the audit review and June 22–24 at the second site to review local gaps. The primary site works for the remaining onboarding visits unless we agree on another location in advance.

Mara agrees to submit expenses within five business days after each visit, with reimbursement within ten business days of submission. She agrees that Trestle will cover up to four hotel nights per visit and arrange and pay for any additional nights a required itinerary needs, approved before booking. Mara will cover extra nights she chooses for personal travel.

The proposed after-hours handover works for Mara, including the five-minute backup trigger and her scheduled sign-off regardless of acknowledgment. I can recommend acceptance once Mara reviews the written offer and confirms that the named primary and backup and their paging schedule cover after-hours response from June 1, including during training.
